_comment: Balance numbers. Never hardcode any of these in logic (CLAUDE.md rule 5). Enemy vision radii and speeds are in data/enemies.json; the detection and alert numbers are here.
_actionPoints: Raised by one from the 2/3/2 of SPEC.md §5's first draft. Hedgerow costs 2 and is the safe artery of §8, so a 2 AP sapper spent his whole turn on a single hedgerow hex and the middle approach was unusable. The scout keeps his +1 over the other roles, which is how §5 stated his edge. Doubling instead would have let a scout cross a third of the map in one turn and taken the pressure out of the 20-turn clock.
_minimumStep: A unit at FULL action points may always move one hex, even into terrain that costs more than its whole pool, spending everything it has. Unused AP is still never banked (SPEC.md §4). This was added when a 2 AP sapper could never enter a 3 AP marsh at all; the pools below now cover that directly, so its remaining job is the wounded trooper of SPEC.md §5, who drops to 1 AP and would otherwise be unable to leave a hedgerow.
_command: The leader's command radius. At the start of each turn a trooper within `radius` hexes of a trooper flagged `leader` in roster.json gets `bonusActionPoints` added to his pool for that turn — he has been given orders. Measured at the moment the pool is filled, so moving next to the leader mid-turn pays off on the following turn. This is a rule, not a trait: it modifies other troopers, and SPEC.md §5's hooks only ever modify their own owner.
_bases: The base values the trait hooks modify (SPEC.md §5, §7, §9). They landed at M3 so every trait can be shown firing against a real number; the systems that act on them — charges and fuses at M5, gunfire at M4/M5, the drop at M6, trooper vision at M4 — arrive later and must read them from here.
_detection: SPEC.md §6: detection = base(enemy) - cover(terrain) - concealment(trooper) + proximity, then the onDetectionCheck trait hook; spotted when it reaches `threshold`. No dice: the hover readout shows exactly this sum. `cover` is keyed by the cover word in data/terrain.json. `proximity[d]` is the bonus at d hexes, past the end of the list it is 0. A trooper is tested on every hex he entered this turn, or on the hex he stands on if he never moved. Starting numbers, for the M8 balance pass: open ground in an arc is spotted, heavy cover is safe unless an enemy is adjacent, and a scout in heavy cover is safe even then.
_alert: SPEC.md §6. Alert is a points total; `states` are the four dial positions and `from` is the points at which each begins, lowest first. At 0/2/4/7 (SPEC.md §6) one event is not a whole state: one sighting leaves the garrison Calm, and the bridge alone (one explosion, +3) leaves it Suspicious. Points are capped at the last state's `from`. `quietTurnsToDecay` turns with no alert raised drop it to the start of the state below, or to 0 in Calm. `visionBonus` is added to every enemy's vision radius in that state. `spotted` is per trooper spotted in a turn, however many enemies saw him.
_patrols: How the alert states move patrols (SPEC.md §6). Suspicious: a patrol stops to sweep on every `suspiciousPauseEvery`-th turn and walks on the others — read literally, 'pause and sweep' would freeze patrols for the rest of the mission once an explosion pins the alert at Suspicious. A sweep turns the patrol `sweepRotation` hex directions (3 is an about-face). Alert: the `alertConverge` nearest moving enemies head for the last known contact. Alarmed: every moving enemy does. Whoever reaches it sweeps, the contact counts as searched, and everyone goes back to their route.
_spotRadius: SPEC.md §5 gives the scout 3 and is silent on the others; 2 was chosen for sappers and gunners. Nothing uses a trooper's spot radius until the gunner's suppress at M5: there is no fog of war (§6).
_concealment: concealment(trooper) in the detection formula. SPEC.md §5: detection against a scout is reduced one step.
